heading: PROPHET YŪNUS (AS)
title: THE CALL IN THE DARKNESS
themes: Tawḥīd • Patience • Duʿāʾ • Accountability • Mercy • Hope • Sincere Change
scope: 8 CONNECTED STORIES | 12 INTERACTIVE MISSIONS | 17 SELECTED QUR’ANIC VERSES
introduction: Volume Twenty-One continues the ʿIBRAH Junior learning journey after Dhū al-Kifl. It concentrates on Prophet Yūnus (peace be upon him), whom the Qur’an explicitly calls one of the messengers (al-Ṣāffāt 37:139). His account is located in several passages, rather than told as a single uninterrupted narrative: 6:86, 10:98, 21:87–88, 37:139–148 and 68:48–50. This volume combines those passages with care; it does not invent scenes, dialogue, dates, a childhood, exact travel routes or details of the great fish.

The historically grounded arc is clear: Yūnus was a Messenger; the Qur’an speaks of his departure, the laden ship, the casting of lots and the great fish; he called upon Allah in the darkness; Allah answered and delivered him, and describes his later illness and a plant that grew by Allah’s command. The Qur’an also honours the repentance and belief of Yūnus’s people and tells us that his Lord chose him among the righteous. The precise reconstruction of every event’s timing is not always stated; where texts are separate, the manuscript does not impose a fictional chronology.

stories.title: The Empty Place on the Shelf
stories.subtitle: Learning begins with what the Qur’an actually says

blocks.text: The blue folder from the children’s previous learning world was almost full. Akhlaq had placed the card marked PATIENCE beside the page about Dhū al-Kifl when Dadi Jaan arrived carrying a small empty file. She set it between two Qur’an bookmarks and said, “Our next story also teaches patience, but we must begin with a name.”

Imaan read the label: YŪNUS. Mohsin leaned across the table. “Isn’t that the Prophet and the giant fish?” Akhlaq quickly drew a fish large enough to swallow the entire notebook. Dadi Jaan smiled, but gently closed the drawing. “Before we make pictures or guesses, open the Qur’an. Al-Ṣāffāt 37:139 tells us that Yūnus was one of the Messengers. Al-Anʿām 6:86 names him among those whom Allah honoured.”

“Then what is the empty file for?” asked Mohsina. “For things we know, and for things we must not pretend to know,” Dadi replied. She handed out cards marked QUR’AN, AUTHENTIC HADITH, TAFSĪR EXPLANATION and MODERN STORY. The children found it surprisingly difficult to sort their favourite bits of the story. Someone had heard that the fish belonged to a certain species. Someone else had heard a number of days. Neither could find those details in the passages they had opened.

Akhlaq was disappointed. “Our exhibition will be boring if we cannot use every detail.” Sheikh Uncle, joining them from the doorway, shook his head. “Knowledge does not become boring because it is accurate. Wonder grows when we recognise what Allah has truly told us.”

At school Sir Zameer announced a new exhibition: MERCY AND NEW BEGINNINGS. Every group would teach one Qur’anic lesson and one everyday action. Team Amanah chose Yūnus (AS). Mohsin offered to make beautiful source cards; Mohsina would check every reference; Imaan would write the family-friendly explanations. Akhlaq volunteered to make a mysterious display with waves and stars, but he agreed there would be no Prophet, ship disaster or fish-swallowing animation.

That evening Akhlaq wrote the first rule on a page headed OUR TRUST: WE DO NOT FILL GAPS IN REVELATION WITH OUR IMAGINATION. He put his drawing aside and drew a careful bookmark instead. The folder was still almost empty. Now, for the first time, the empty space felt like a responsibility rather than a problem.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: Tell sacred history accurately and acknowledge what we do not know.

stories.title: The Warning Nobody Wanted
stories.subtitle: Speaking wisely when others do not listen

blocks.text: At the academy a new bookshelf had been placed near the corridor. There were signs asking pupils not to leave bags in the narrow walkway, but by the second day the space was crowded again. Mohsina noticed a younger pupil struggling to pass and asked Sir Zameer whether the team could help explain the rule.

Akhlaq wanted to stand in the corridor and shout, “Everybody must listen to us!” Imaan suggested something simpler: move their own things, ask the teacher to announce the rule, and offer help to pupils who had not understood where bags belonged. “If we are rude,” she said, “the message may be right, but our manners will be wrong.”

That afternoon Sheikh Uncle opened the Qur’an to passages about Yūnus (AS). The Qur’an says he was a Messenger and speaks of the people who eventually believed. It also describes a serious moment in his own story. “Do we know the exact conversations he had with each person?” Sheikh Uncle asked. Everyone shook their head. “Then we must not write speeches for him or invent a classroom scene in his lifetime. But we can learn how valuable it is to take truthful guidance seriously.”

The next morning Team Amanah made a small sign: KEEP THE PATH CLEAR SO EVERYONE CAN PASS. They demonstrated where bags could go and helped move their own books first. Some pupils listened. Two did not, and one laughed at the sign. Akhlaq’s cheeks warmed. He wanted to take down the whole display.

Sir Zameer quietly said, “People may reject a sensible request. That does not make shouting the solution. We can remain clear, respectful and consistent, then ask an adult to enforce a safety rule.” The teacher dealt with the remaining bags without humiliating anyone. A pupil who had laughed earlier returned later to offer help.

At home Akhlaq admitted that he had wanted everyone to change immediately. Dadi Jaan reminded him that no child can control another person’s heart. “Do your responsibility well,” she said. “Ask for support when needed. Don’t confuse a sincere effort with guaranteed obedience from everyone.”

When the children checked the corridor on Friday, the path was open. Akhlaq did not write WE MADE EVERYONE GOOD. He wrote something smaller and truer: WE SPOKE RESPECTFULLY, ACTED FIRST AND ASKED FOR HELP.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: Offer guidance gently; we cannot control another person’s response.

stories.title: The Boat on the Noticeboard
stories.subtitle: Pausing before a decision and staying within the evidence

blocks.text: The exhibition team wanted to create a timeline board showing what the Qur’an says about Yūnus (AS). Mohsin cut blue paper for the sea, while Akhlaq placed a little cardboard boat in the centre. Imaan checked al-Ṣāffāt 37:140–142: the passage speaks of a laden ship, a drawing of lots and the great fish. It gave them enough to make a respectful text diagram without acting out the event.

Akhlaq suddenly proposed a game. “What if the player has to jump into the sea to escape the fish?” Mohsina stared at him. “That isn’t what we are learning, and we should never make dangerous choices into fun rewards.” Sir Zameer agreed. A sacred trial was not a survival game, and nobody should imagine that a child must risk their safety to show courage.

They redesigned the board. Instead of moving a pretend human through danger, the learner would place three text cards in source order: LADEN SHIP, CASTING OF LOTS, GREAT FISH. A separate card would ask which details had actually been stated in the Qur’an. The fish would not be a monster to defeat; the Prophet would not be an avatar.

Later that day a different decision challenged Akhlaq. The group’s model was not finished, and he was tired of waiting for the glue to dry. “I’ll carry it to the exhibition table now,” he said. Imaan warned that the pieces would shift. He took two steps, watched one corner bend, and stopped.

He was irritated. “If I wait for everything, nothing gets done!” Mohsina suggested asking their teacher to approve a faster drying method. They moved the board onto a safe shelf instead of rushing. The next day its edges were straight.

That evening Salaam spoke with the children about the difference between a modern craft mistake and the account of a Prophet. “We are not saying your impatient glue experiment is equal to what Yūnus experienced,” he reminded them. “We are practising only a small, separate lesson: when your emotions grow strong, pause and seek sound guidance before you act.”
Akhlaq wrote PAUSE, CHECK, ASK, THEN ACT beneath the boat diagram. The display had become less dramatic. It had also become truthful, safe and much more useful.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: When emotions are strong, pause, check and seek wise help before acting.

stories.title: Words for the Darkest Moment
stories.subtitle: Tawḥīd, sincere duʿāʾ and honest repair

blocks.text: A heavy rainstorm interrupted afternoon activities at the academy. The lights briefly went out, and Sir Zameer calmly led the younger children to the supervised classroom area. Nobody was trapped or hurt, but Akhlaq felt unsettled by the sudden darkness. He was relieved when the emergency lights came on.

While waiting for the rain to settle, Dadi Jaan—who had come to collect the siblings—read the meaning of al-Anbiyāʾ 21:87. She explained that Yūnus (AS) called upon Allah in the darkness with words that declared Allah alone worthy of worship, glorified Him and acknowledged wrongdoing. She recited slowly: Lā ilāha illā Anta, subḥānaka, innī kuntu minaẓ-ẓālimīn.

Akhlaq repeated the words quietly. “So we can make duʿāʾ when we are afraid?” he asked. “Of course,” Dadi replied. “And we can also follow our teacher’s safety instructions, ask for help and rest when we need to.” She reminded them that Allah’s response to a person’s prayer should not be turned into a promise that all difficulty ends immediately.

When the rain passed, the class returned to the exhibition tables. Mohsin discovered a card was missing from the source folder. Akhlaq remembered taking it home to practise reading the Arabic. He had intended to bring it back, but forgotten. Nobody accused him, and he could have remained silent. Instead, he stood beside Sir Zameer and said, “I took the card with permission, but I forgot to return it. I’m sorry. I can bring it tomorrow and help make a temporary copy today.”

The teacher thanked him for speaking clearly. “Acknowledging wrong is an important beginning,” he said. “Repairing what you can is another step.” Imaan helped prepare a replacement card with the correct reference while Mohsina made a checklist for borrowed materials.

At home Akhlaq opened his notebook to the duʿāʾ again. He understood that its power was not a magic way to avoid consequences. It was worship, turning sincerely to Allah. He had also learned not to hide a small mistake simply because the truth felt uncomfortable.
He added two lines below the Arabic words: ASK ALLAH FOR HELP. TELL THE TRUTH AND REPAIR WHAT I CAN.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: Turn to Allah sincerely and repair mistakes with truthful action.

stories.title: When Help Arrives Quietly
stories.subtitle: Mercy, recovery and caring without false promises

blocks.text: Several days later the academy announced that a younger pupil had been unwell and would return for short lessons while recovering. The class wanted to prepare a huge welcome party with loud music and an hour of games. Mohsina hesitated. “What if the pupil is tired? We should ask what would actually help.”

They spoke with the teacher, who had permission to share only practical information: the pupil needed a quieter place, shorter activities and a way to leave early. The team prepared a comfortable reading corner instead of a noisy celebration. Nobody asked the child to describe private medical details.

In the Qur’an lesson Sir Zameer read al-Ṣāffāt 37:145–146. After Allah delivered Yūnus (AS), the Qur’an says he was cast onto open land while ill and that Allah caused a gourd-type plant to grow over him. The children were moved by the account of care and mercy. Sir Zameer cautioned them not to invent how the plant was used or create an unverified medical treatment from the verse.

“So Allah cared for him when he was weak,” Imaan said. “Yes,” replied Sir Zameer. “And in our own lives we should treat people who are recovering with patience, dignity and practical care. But an ill person should also receive appropriate professional help; duʿāʾ does not replace treatment.”

When the pupil returned, Akhlaq offered a seat but did not insist on conversation. Mohsin brought a light book. Mohsina checked whether the path to the door was clear. Imaan asked the teacher which activities the pupil wished to join. Some plans were postponed without fuss.

Later Akhlaq realised he had wanted to be the hero of the welcome. “I thought a great welcome meant making everyone excited,” he admitted. “Sometimes,” said Salamah at dinner, “the kindest help is quiet, unannounced and shaped around the other person’s actual needs.”

The next day the pupil stayed for a few minutes longer and smiled at the reading corner. The children did not write WE MADE HIM WELL. They wrote WE OFFERED CARE AND LET HIM CHOOSE. Their poster now had a new card beside HOPE: MERCY RESPECTS A PERSON’S NEEDS.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: Help someone recovering without making promises about their health.

stories.title: The Classroom That Chose to Change
stories.subtitle: A community’s repentance should become action

blocks.text: The school’s shared garden had become untidy. Some pupils had dropped wrappers, and several groups blamed one another. A class meeting dissolved into arguments. “Why should we clean the mess?” Mohsin asked. “We did not make all of it.” Akhlaq agreed, until Imaan asked whether the arguing would make the garden better.

That afternoon Dadi Jaan read the meaning of Yūnus 10:98. The people of Yūnus believed, and Allah removed the punishment that had threatened them. She explained that their acceptance of the truth was a distinctive mercy reported by the Qur’an. “We are not pretending a messy garden is comparable to punishment described in revelation,” she said. “But we can learn that a community is not required to remain in its wrong habits forever.”

The children returned to school with a proposal. Instead of naming and shaming a group, they would ask each class to make one voluntary change. The oldest pupils would help set up labelled bins; younger pupils would learn where wrappers belonged; volunteers would clean with suitable gloves and adult supervision. Sir Zameer arranged proper disposal and told them not to touch sharp or unsafe waste.

Akhlaq knew he had dropped a wrapper outside the garden once. He wanted to avoid mentioning it. Then he said to his teammates, “I have been careless before. I will put my own things right and use the bin.” Nobody held a public confession ceremony. Mohsin acknowledged that he had laughed when another child left litter. He offered to help restore the garden bed.

By the following week, the path was clearer. There were still mistakes and reminders, but the overall behaviour had changed. The children kept the bins accessible and asked the staff how to maintain them. “A new beginning is not only a poster,” Mohsina said. “It means keeping up the good work.”

At the exhibition, Team Amanah put two columns on the board: WE USED TO IGNORE and WE NOW PRACTISE. They chose behaviours rather than names. Akhlaq felt proud, but Sheikh Uncle reminded him that a child cannot measure repentance in someone’s heart. “We can see actions and encourage better ones. Allah knows what is sincere.”
Akhlaq added the words CHANGE IS SHOWN THROUGH ACTION. This was not a claim that he could guarantee anyone’s future. It was a promise to begin with his own conduct.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: A community can choose better habits; repentance requires sincerity and change.

stories.title: A Second Chance for Team Amanah
stories.subtitle: Patience, dignity and repairing a broken trust

blocks.text: Two days before the final exhibition, the team discovered that the entire first draft of its presentation had been printed with the wrong reference beside one Qur’anic meaning card. The mistake had begun when Akhlaq copied the wrong number from his notebook and the others trusted the sheet without checking.

Mohsin was frustrated. “We have to start again! We should have used a different writer.” Akhlaq felt his stomach sink. He was ready to leave the room. Then Imaan pointed at the sign from their third story: PAUSE, CHECK, ASK, THEN ACT.

Sir Zameer did not blame a single child publicly. He asked the team to check each source independently, correct the printed card and make a new verification list. The children divided the work. Mohsina confirmed the Arabic text against the approved source folder; Imaan checked the meaning guide; Mohsin revised the design; Akhlaq read the final citations aloud to an adult before printing.

During the lesson Sheikh Uncle read al-Qalam 68:48–50, which calls for patience and recalls the companion of the fish. The final verse states that Allah chose him and made him among the righteous. “Always tell the complete account,” Sheikh Uncle instructed. “We must never speak disrespectfully of Yūnus (AS) or reduce a Messenger to the moment of trial. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ also taught people not to claim superiority over Yūnus ibn Mattā.”

Akhlaq asked whether accepting responsibility meant being ashamed forever. “No,” answered Sheikh Uncle. “You can admit the error, put it right, learn from it and continue. But you must not use forgiveness as an excuse to avoid repairing harm.”

The new printout was smaller and clearer. They placed the source verification checklist in the teacher’s drawer so future classes could use it. When a younger pupil asked why one label had been covered with a corrected version, Akhlaq answered plainly: “We found an error and fixed it before teaching others.”

The team was not rewarded with an invisible faith score. They were relieved to know their exhibit would not mislead readers. The true achievement was a more careful habit: every important claim should be checked before it is passed along.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: Patience includes correcting errors and respecting those whom Allah honoured.

stories.title: The Card After the Storm
stories.subtitle: What remains when the exhibition is over

blocks.text: The exhibition opened on a bright morning. The school hall had a simple sea-coloured background, carefully printed Qur’anic references, and an empty space where children could write one private promise for themselves. No figure of a Prophet appeared, and the great fish was not a game character. Instead, visitors followed the source cards and then tried safe decisions from everyday life.

Dadi Jaan visited first. “Tell me the most important thing you learned,” she asked. Mohsin said, “A Qur’anic account must be told accurately.” Mohsina said, “Mercy includes making room for someone who needs help.” Imaan said, “People can change when they turn sincerely to Allah and choose better actions.”

Akhlaq looked at the final card. He could have named the ship, the fish or the plant. Instead, he recited slowly: “Lā ilāha illā Anta, subḥānaka, innī kuntu minaẓ-ẓālimīn.” He knew he was repeating the Qur’anic supplication of Yūnus (AS), not performing a scene from his life. “It reminds me to turn to Allah and admit when I am wrong,” he said.

Sheikh Uncle asked one further question: “When should a child ask another person for help?” The children answered together: when something is dangerous, unfair, frightening, or too difficult to handle alone. Duʿāʾ and seeking help are not enemies. A child who needs protection must never be left alone with that burden.

At the end of the day the school asked every group to name a practice it could keep without awards or applause. Team Amanah chose one: CHECK THE FACTS, SPEAK GENTLY, REPAIR MISTAKES. They placed this beside the Qur’anic words of hope, patience and mercy.

At home, Akhlaq put his notebook beside the family tree and the folders from their earlier journeys. Dadi Jaan gave him a final blank bookmark: THE NEXT STORY BEGINS WITH A QUIET PRAYER. He smiled. There would be another Prophet to learn about, another journey through authentic revelation, and more ordinary days in which the children could practise its lessons.
He did not try to make the compass glow. He simply left the bookmark ready. The most important direction was already clear: remember Allah, keep learning, and make one good choice at a time.

blocks.label: CARRY FORWARD
blocks.text: Carry forward Tawḥīd, duʿāʾ, mercy, patient action and honest repair.

missions.title: A Messenger Worth Honouring

discover.text: The Qur’an calls Yūnus one of the Messengers. Another passage honours him alongside other servants of Allah. Our curiosity about the story must never remove our respect for the Prophet.

missions.question: A friend wants to invent funny dialogue for Yūnus to make the exhibition popular.

choices.text: Explain that we cannot invent words for a Prophet and suggest a truthful source card.
choices.feedback: Respectful learning uses what revelation supports, not imagined speech.

choices.text: Write the invented speech but label it “probably true.”
choices.feedback: “Probably true” cannot turn invented dialogue into revelation. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Stop learning because every historical detail is not available.
choices.feedback: Learning the authentic account is valuable even when it leaves some details unstated. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.action: Tell one person an accurately sourced fact about Yūnus (AS), in a respectful manner.

missions.title: Listening Before Dismissing

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Recognise that accepting truthful guidance matters and that sincere change is possible.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 10:98. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The Qur’an records the people of Yūnus coming to belief and Allah removing a worldly punishment. A modern classroom rule is not the same as their experience; the limited lesson is to consider sound correction seriously.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: Do I ignore helpful advice only because I dislike hearing it?

evidence.arabic: فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

evidence.arabic: فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

missions.question: A teacher asks pupils to keep a path clear for someone who needs more space.

choices.text: Laugh because other people ignore the instruction.
choices.feedback: Mocking a necessary safety instruction can harm others. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Listen, help clear the path and ask questions respectfully if unsure.
choices.feedback: Correct action begins with listening and responding responsibly.

choices.text: Tell the teacher the rule is useless because it was broken yesterday.
choices.feedback: A rule can still be useful even when people have ignored it before. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.title: When Your Advice Is Ignored

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 68:48. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The Qur’an commands patience and recalls Yūnus’s trial; it does not require a child to tolerate unsafe treatment. We may remain respectful, set boundaries and involve a safe adult.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: How do I respond when others do not immediately agree with me?

choices.text: Explain the concern once, then ask a teacher to handle the safety issue.

choices.feedback: Anger does not justify unfair blame. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.title: What the Ship Passage Actually Says

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Distinguish Qur’anic facts from invented narrative detail.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 37:140–142. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The passage mentions the heavily laden ship, drawing of lots and the great fish. It does not tell us a boat name, a species or a precise duration. Knowledge is a trust.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: Have I repeated a fascinating detail without checking its source?

evidence.arabic: وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ
evidence.meaning: Yūnus was certainly one of Allah’s messengers.

evidence.arabic: إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ
evidence.meaning: The Qur’an recalls his departure to a heavily laden ship.

evidence.arabic: فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُدْحَضِينَ
evidence.meaning: Lots were drawn, and his lot was among those that lost.

evidence.arabic: فَالْتَقَمَهُ الْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ
evidence.meaning: The great fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy for his departure.

missions.question: A classmate writes, “Yūnus remained inside the fish exactly three days,” as a confirmed Qur’anic fact.

choices.text: Keep it because a precise number makes a better story.
choices.feedback: The Qur’an does not establish that exact number. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Remove the unsupported claim and explain what the Qur’an actually states.
choices.feedback: Source accuracy matters more than a dramatic detail.

choices.text: Make up a different number to show it is uncertain.
choices.feedback: Replacing one unsupported number with another does not correct the problem. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.action: Correct one uncertain fact in your school notes using a reliable source.

remember.label: REMEMBER — PRIVATE MUḤĀSABAH
remember.text: Have I repeated a fascinating detail without checking its source? Offer “Practised / Still learning / Skip” without collecting private confession data or public faith scores.

remember.label: VOCABULARY
remember.text: الْفُلْك — ship; الْحُوت — great fish

missions.title: The Duʿāʾ in the Darkness

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Recognise the Qur’anic duʿāʾ as Tawḥīd, tasbīḥ and acknowledgment of wrong.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 21:87. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: Yūnus called on Allah alone: “There is no deity except You; You are free of imperfection; I was among those who wronged.” This is worship, not a magical command or a guarantee of a particular immediate outcome.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: When I am worried, do I remember that I can ask Allah for help and also seek safe human support?

evidence.arabic: وَذَا النُّونِ إِذْ ذَهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
evidence.meaning: The companion of the fish called on Allah in the darkness, declaring Tawḥīd, glorifying Him and admitting his own wrong. The clause before his duʿāʾ needs careful classical explanation.

evidence.arabic: فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ
evidence.meaning: The Qur’an points to his glorification of Allah.

missions.question: A child feels afraid during a brief power failure at school.

choices.text: Hide from every adult and promise not to tell anyone.
choices.feedback: A child should not isolate themselves during a frightening safety event. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Assume that making duʿāʾ means safety procedures are unnecessary.
choices.feedback: Duʿāʾ does not cancel the need for sensible safety action. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Stay with a trusted teacher, follow instructions and make duʿāʾ.
choices.feedback: Duʿāʾ and safe practical action can go together.

missions.action: Recite the supplication with understanding, voluntarily and with caregiver guidance.

remember.label: REMEMBER — PRIVATE MUḤĀSABAH
remember.text: When I am worried, do I remember that I can ask Allah for help and also seek safe human support? Offer “Practised / Still learning / Skip” without collecting private confession data or public faith scores.

remember.label: VOCABULARY
remember.text: سُبْحَانَكَ — glory be to You; الظَّالِمِينَ — those who wronged

missions.title: Truthful Repair

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Learn that acknowledging a mistake should lead to appropriate repair.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 21:87. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: In his duʿāʾ Yūnus humbly acknowledged wrongdoing. Children can learn that honesty is a beginning, followed by making amends where possible. No child must reveal private sins to an app.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: What can I repair when I have made a small mistake?

evidence.arabic: وَذَا النُّونِ إِذْ ذَهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
evidence.meaning: The companion of the fish called on Allah in the darkness, declaring Tawḥīd, glorifying Him and admitting his own wrong. The clause before his duʿāʾ needs careful classical explanation.

evidence.arabic: فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
evidence.meaning: Allah answered him and rescued him from distress; the verse also teaches hope in Allah’s help for believers.

missions.question: Akhlaq borrowed a source card with permission and forgot to bring it back.

choices.text: Admit he forgot, help make a temporary copy and return it.
choices.feedback: Honesty plus repair helps restore trust.

choices.text: Say somebody else must have misplaced it.
choices.feedback: An unfounded accusation adds another wrong. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Stay silent so no one feels annoyed.
choices.feedback: Silence prevents the team from solving the problem. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.action: Make one small, age-appropriate correction if needed; do not enter personal confessions in the app.

missions.title: Allah Answered

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Understand hope in Allah’s mercy without promising identical outcomes for everyone.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 21:88. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The Qur’an says Allah answered Yūnus and rescued him from anguish. This encourages trust in Allah. We cannot promise that every hardship ends quickly or that asking for help shows weak faith.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: Can I show hope while still seeking support when I need it?

evidence.arabic: فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
evidence.meaning: Allah answered him and rescued him from distress; the verse also teaches hope in Allah’s help for believers.

evidence.arabic: فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ
evidence.meaning: The Qur’an points to his glorification of Allah.

evidence.arabic: لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
evidence.meaning: Without Allah’s mercy connected to his glorification, he would have remained there until the resurrection.

evidence.arabic: فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ
evidence.meaning: Allah cast him onto an open shore while he was ill.

missions.question: Mohsina knows a friend is worried about a family difficulty.

choices.text: Promise the problem will disappear tomorrow.
choices.feedback: We cannot guarantee how or when a worldly problem will resolve. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Offer respectful support, make duʿāʾ and suggest a trusted adult if help is needed.
choices.feedback: Compassion respects privacy and does not make promises about an unknown outcome.

choices.text: Ask the friend for every private detail so the class can help.
choices.feedback: People should not be pressured to disclose private distress. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.action: Offer one kind action and an appropriate duʿāʾ without asking for private explanations.

remember.label: REMEMBER — PRIVATE MUḤĀSABAH
remember.text: Can I show hope while still seeking support when I need it? Offer “Practised / Still learning / Skip” without collecting private confession data or public faith scores.

missions.title: Care for Someone Recovering

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Recognise Allah’s care and practise respectful support for someone unwell.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 37:145–146. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The Qur’an reports Yūnus arriving ill on open ground and Allah causing a gourd-type plant to grow. We must not turn this into unverified medical claims. Children can practise useful, respectful care.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: Do I ask what someone needs rather than deciding for them?

evidence.arabic: فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
evidence.meaning: Allah answered him and rescued him from distress; the verse also teaches hope in Allah’s help for believers.

evidence.arabic: فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ
evidence.meaning: Allah cast him onto an open shore while he was ill.

evidence.arabic: وَأَنْبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِنْ يَقْطِينٍ
evidence.meaning: Allah caused a gourd-type plant to grow over him.

missions.question: A classmate returns after illness and needs a quieter place.

choices.text: Plan a loud surprise party without asking.
choices.feedback: A surprise may overwhelm someone who is recovering. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Say the classmate must be completely healthy because they returned.
choices.feedback: Returning to class does not mean a person needs no further support. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Ask the teacher what support is suitable and offer a calm, flexible welcome.
choices.feedback: Good care follows the person’s needs and respects medical guidance and privacy.

missions.action: Offer a gentle, appropriate kindness to someone with adult permission.

remember.text: Do I ask what someone needs rather than deciding for them? Offer “Practised / Still learning / Skip” without collecting private confession data or public faith scores.

remember.text: سَقِيمٌ — ill; يَقْطِين — gourd-type plant

missions.title: When a Community Changes

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Understand belief, repentance and meaningful reform without public shaming.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 10:98. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The people of Yūnus believed and Allah gave them respite. Their response was a special Qur’anic event, not an ordinary classroom clean-up. The limited practical lesson is to replace bad habits with sincere, observable change.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: Do my apologies lead to better habits?

evidence.arabic: فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
evidence.meaning: The people of Yūnus believed; Allah removed from them a humiliating worldly punishment and allowed them respite.

evidence.arabic: وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
evidence.meaning: Allah sent him to a people numbering one hundred thousand or more.

evidence.arabic: فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
evidence.meaning: They believed and were permitted enjoyment for an appointed time.

missions.question: A school garden is untidy and pupils are blaming one another.

choices.text: Name and shame the children most likely responsible.
choices.feedback: Public humiliation does not teach fair accountability. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Join a supervised improvement plan, correct your own habits and treat others fairly.
choices.feedback: Real improvement requires action while respecting the dignity of others.

choices.text: Announce everyone has repented even though nothing has changed.
choices.feedback: We cannot know or award the spiritual state of another person. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.action: Choose one small positive habit and practise it for the next week.

missions.title: Beginning Again with Integrity

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Respond to correction with renewed responsibility and respect.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 37:148. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE
discover.text: The Qur’an tells us of belief among the people and of Allah choosing Yūnus among the righteous. We must not collapse these verses into one invented scene. Everyday learning can include correcting mistakes and persevering.

discover.label: REFLECT — A QUESTION TO CARRY
discover.text: When I discover an error, do I hide it or put it right?

evidence.arabic: فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

evidence.arabic: فَاجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
evidence.meaning: His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.

missions.question: The team finds a wrong verse number on a printed exhibition card.

choices.text: Leave it because changing it may be embarrassing.
choices.feedback: A wrong religious reference should not be knowingly published. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Blame the youngest volunteer without evidence.
choices.feedback: Unfair blame does not improve accuracy. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Check the source, correct the reference and improve the review process.
choices.feedback: Integrity turns a discovered error into careful correction.

missions.action: Re-check one fact before teaching it to another person.

missions.title: The Lesson We Carry Forward

discover.label: LEARNING TARGET
discover.text: Bring together patience, Tawḥīd, dignity, mercy and practical action.

discover.label: DISCOVER — THE QUR’AN
discover.text: 68:48–50. Study the selected complete āyah / āyāt in Part I. Arabic and approved final meaning are displayed together in the app.

discover.label: UNDERSTAND — EXPLAINING THE GUIDANCE

evidence.arabic: فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
evidence.meaning: Allah answered him and rescued him from distress; the verse also teaches hope in Allah’s help for believers.

evidence.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُنْ كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ
evidence.meaning: The Qur’an gives a command to be patient and recalls the distressed call of the companion of the fish.

evidence.arabic: لَوْلَا أَنْ تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ

missions.question: The exhibition is over, and Akhlaq must choose how to continue learning.

choices.text: Choose one realistic action: check facts, speak respectfully or repair a mistake.
choices.feedback: Small, sincere and safe actions are better than impossible promises or ranking others.

choices.text: Promise never to feel angry or make an error again.
choices.feedback: Children may feel anger or make mistakes; the goal is responsible response. Review the core verse and try again.

choices.text: Rate classmates from “least faithful” to “most faithful.”
choices.feedback: Only Allah knows hearts; public spiritual ranking is inappropriate. Review the core verse and try again.

missions.action: Write or privately choose one realistic “carry forward” practice for seven days.

review.meaning: The Qur’an gives a command to be patient and recalls the distressed call of the companion of the fish.

review.arabic: لَوْلَا أَنْ تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ
review.meaning: Allah’s grace reached him; without that grace the outcome would have been blameworthy.
His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.

synthesis.text: What the Qur’an establishes

Yūnus (AS) was one of Allah’s messengers (37:139), is named among those specially favoured (6:86), and is honoured as chosen and righteous (68:50). Allah relates his difficult departure, the laden ship and drawing of lots, the great fish, and his supplication in the darkness (21:87; 37:140–144). Allah answered and rescued him (21:88), describes his illness and the plant grown for him (37:145–146), and records the belief and respite of his people (10:98; 37:147–148). The Qur’an commands patience when recalling the companion of the fish (68:48–49).
Eight lasting lessons for children
Tawḥīd: turn sincerely to Allah alone in worship and duʿāʾ.
Respect: honour the Prophets and do not turn sacred events into fiction.
Truth: distinguish Qur’anic facts from attractive but unsupported details.
Patience: pause before an unsafe or unfair response; seek sensible help.
Accountability: admit a wrong without excuses and repair what you can.
Mercy: make room for people who are weak, recovering or learning.
New beginnings: real change appears in choices and continuing habits.
Hope: trust Allah while accepting that outcomes and timings belong to His wisdom.
One-week family character practice
Day
Voluntary child-friendly practice
Caregiver prompt
Check one story detail against an authentic source.
Where did we find this fact?
Make one helpful request politely and listen carefully.
How can we speak clearly without shaming?
Pause before one hurried decision.
Would checking first make it safer?
Recite or listen to Yūnus’s duʿāʾ and learn its meaning.
What do these words say about Allah?
Offer an appropriate small kindness to a person needing support.
What help would the person actually welcome?
Correct one harmless mistake without blaming others.
How can we put this right?
Choose one sustainable practice to carry forward.
What small action can we continue next week?
Final knowledge and character assessment
CHECK • What confirms that Yūnus was a Messenger? ANSWER GUIDE • Qur’an 37:139.
CHECK • Which passage contains his supplication in the darkness? ANSWER GUIDE • Qur’an 21:87.
CHECK • What are the three core meanings of this supplication? ANSWER GUIDE • Tawḥīd, glorification of Allah and acknowledging wrongdoing.
CHECK • Which verses record the rescue? ANSWER GUIDE • Qur’an 21:88 and 37:143–145, among related passages.
CHECK • What does the Qur’an say about his people? ANSWER GUIDE • They believed and Allah gave them respite; 10:98 and 37:148.
CHECK • Which account details must not be invented? ANSWER GUIDE • Species of the fish, length of time inside, the ship’s name, unsourced speeches or scenes.
CHECK • How can a person respond to a wrong? ANSWER GUIDE • Acknowledge it, seek help when needed, repair reasonably and try again.
CHECK • Can an app measure who is most loved by Allah? ANSWER GUIDE • No. The app tracks completed learning activities, never a person’s spiritual rank.

CLOSING REFLECTION • I honour Yūnus (AS) as a Messenger, turn to Allah in duʿāʾ, check what revelation actually says, and choose one good action today. When I struggle, I may seek trusted help, repair mistakes and begin again.
